At the community center, Maria notices Cheryl looking stressed and overwhelmed with the stacks of paperwork and planning needed for a new community outreach project.

Maria: I thought so. Would you like some help with that? I’ve got some time to spare and I’d be happy to assist you.

steps.raw_response:
Perspective: Maria Ortega.

From my own viewpoint, I first helped Cheryl because I saw her stressed and overwhelmed, and I had time to spare. Afterward, I noticed she was handling responsibilities better and seemed more confident. That made me want to support her further, so during the staff meeting I suggested Cheryl lead the next phase. My intention there was to recognize her growth and give her an opportunity.

Then I began to question how that suggestion might have felt to Cheryl. Even though she accepted it, I worried she might have perceived my public nomination as pressure or as me overstepping into her choices. I did not know for certain how she felt; I only had my concern about her possible reaction. That concern changed my intention: instead of only advocating for her leadership, I wanted to check in privately, clarify my support, and make sure she did not feel pushed.

So the shift was driven by my worry about Cheryl’s perception and my concern that I might have overstepped. My later conversation with her, where she said she was surprised but appreciated my support, confirmed that checking in was the right way to protect our trust and partnership.

steps.raw_response:
Perspective: Cheryl Benallie.

From my own viewpoint, I was overwhelmed by the paperwork and planning for the outreach project when Maria offered to help. I accepted because I genuinely needed it. After working with her, I felt more able to handle the responsibilities and more confident in what I was doing.

At the staff meeting, Maria suggested I lead the next phase. I was surprised, but I also felt ready and grateful that she believed in me. I did not experience it as pressure or overstepping; I saw it as support.

Later, Maria came to me privately and said she wanted to make sure I felt supported and not pressured. That told me she had been worried about how her public suggestion might have landed for me. From my side, her intention seemed to shift from nominating me in front of the team to checking in with me personally so she could protect our trust and make sure I was comfortable.

I was a bit surprised by her concern, but I appreciated it. When she suggested we co-lead together, I saw that as a natural continuation of her support. I value working with Maria and want to keep collaborating with her.
